title: Endurance auto warranty services denied my claim.  My $10,000 mistake.
summary: A customer whose Endurance auto warranty denied an engine/turbo claim describes the denial reasons, lack of written documentation, and a settlement offer with a non-disparagement and rights-waiver clause.

assertions.quote: our inspector went out and said that your engine's oily so we think you oil

verdicts.note: Vendor-assigned inspectors routinely assess claims and companies commonly rely on their own findings, but such denials are frequently contested as self-serving rather than being a settled, universal truth

assertions.quote: they will not send you any paperwork they won't put anything in writing

verdicts.note: Withholding written denial reasons is a commonly reported practice among some warranty administrators but is not true of all providers, many of which do send denial letters
Offering a premium refund instead of honoring a claim is a known settlement tactic reported across multiple warranty-complaint accounts, though not universal

assertions.quote: black agrees to wave any and all claims

verdicts.note: Release-and-settlement agreements routinely include broad waiver and complaint-withdrawal clauses, a standard feature of consumer settlement contracts generally, not specific to this company

assertions.quote: statement including those made by digital means that disparage defame or in any way criticize the personal or business reputations

verdicts.note: Non-disparagement clauses are a standard, legally common feature of settlement releases across many industries

assertions.quote: it's hard to find somebody that will accept

verdicts.note: Warranty administrators maintain informal acceptance networks and many independent shops decline third-party warranty work over payment and parts disputes, a widely reported friction point

assertions.quote: mandatory search charge four-wheel drive and turbos so I paid extra for that

verdicts.note: Added surcharges for higher-risk components like turbochargers and 4WD systems are a standard underwriting practice in the vehicle service contract industry
